page.description: openSUSE Leap editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: The stable openSUSE release, built from SUSE's enterprise code base and supported for years rather than months. Pick the offline installer, then the architecture.
pros: A slow-moving, long-lived release rather than a rolling one.
YaST and zypper cover installation, updates and system configuration.
Snapshot rollback on the default Btrfs layout in recent releases.
Installer images for x86_64 and aarch64.
cons: Newer software arrives later than in Tumbleweed.
This publisher signs its media with SHA-512 only, so USB preparation is not offered for it here.
The Commons screenshot shows Leap 15.4, not 16.0.
SUSE's enterprise base means some community packages lag.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of openSUSE Leap 15.4 with GNOME from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 16.0 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: openSUSE Leap 15.4 GNOME desktop with the activities overview
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of openSUSE Leap 15.4 · not 16.0, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: One path per architecture: the offline installer ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. openSUSE publishes SHA-512 for these images, so ROMinit offers the download but not USB preparation.
